MARKET.head: Guangdong lychee ice wine sells out online after APEC dinner menu
MARKET.summ: A Guangdong lychee wine became an unexpected online hit after it was served alongside two Changyu wines at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen, with its producer reporting a more than 93,000% jump in revenue at one online store
takeaways: Yueli Lychee Ice Wine, from Guangzhou ShunChangYuan, was served at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen on November 18.
After the menu circulated online, one Yueli flagship store reportedly received about 5,000 orders within two hours.
The producer reported a 93,393.10% revenue rise at one online store, though the comparison period was not specified.

MARKET.head: VinePair weekly roundup flags Jim Beam pause, record-low wine output, and other industry news
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on the continued production pause at Jim Beam’s main facility, dismal estimates for the 2026 global wine...
takeaways: Jim Beam's main facility remains in a continued production pause, per VinePair's weekly roundup.
VinePair's estimates put 2026 global wine production at dismal, record-low levels.
The same roundup also covered product releases and other beverage alcohol industry updates this week.

MARKET.head: Château Lynch-Bages releases charity labels honouring Hong Kong panda twins
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux classified growth Château Lynch-Bages has released limited-edition wines featuring Hong Kong’s first giant panda twins, pairing a celebration of their birth with fundraising for panda conservation
takeaways: Bordeaux classified growth Château Lynch-Bages released limited-edition 2024 wines with labels featuring Hong Kong's giant panda twins, Jia Jia and De De.
Ocean Park partnered on the commemorative labels, and a charity auction of large-format bottles will fund the park's panda conservation and education programs.
The labels appear on Lynch-Bages and second wine Echo de Lynch-Bages, sold in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau through selected retailers.

MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under one new managing director
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: DBR Lafite appointed Leo Wang, former Pernod Ricard China vice-president, as managing director of Domaine de Long Dai and the Chinese market.
The move unites Long Dai winery management and the national sales team under one executive for the first time.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, nine years at the estate, leaves at year end and will help with the handover.

MARKET.head: Melbourne Polytechnic cuts viticulture degree fees to $4,908 a year from 2027
MARKET.summ: Melbourne Polytechnic is expanding access to tertiary viticulture and winemaking education through Commonwealth Supported Places in its Bachelor of Agriculture and Technology (Viticulture and Winemaking) from 2027. As Victoria's only provider of undergraduate degrees in viticulture and winemaking, Melbourne Polytechnic “plays a...
takeaways: Melbourne Polytechnic will offer Commonwealth Supported Places in its viticulture and winemaking degree from 2027.
Annual student contribution for eligible domestic students drops from $23,160 to $4,908, the only such degree in Victoria.
Victorian Wine Show offers a $5,000 annual scholarship; applications for the 2027 intake are now open.

MARKET.head: WineGB to exhibit English and Welsh wines at Amsterdam trade fair in 2027
MARKET.summ: English and Welsh wine has moved from a niche market to one of the most dynamic cool climate categories in Europe. Producers are gaining international attention for sparkling wines, as
takeaways: WineGB, the English and Welsh wine trade body, will exhibit at Wine Professional in Amsterdam in January 2027.
The stand is run with the UK government's GREAT international comms programme and aims to reach Dutch buyers, importers and sommeliers.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie for North American marketing
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission named Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico and Central America.
She previously led the Center for Produce Safety as chief executive and was international marketing director at American Pistachio Growers.
In the role she will oversee commission promotions and work with importers and retailers to increase demand for fresh California table grapes.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia opens funding call for innovative grape sector projects
MARKET.summ: Wine Australia is today launching a competitive call for innovative eligible projects to secure funding from the Research & Innovation Fund (RIF) which is part of the Australian Wine Future Fund (AWFF). The organisation said innovative and groundbreaking projects tackling the wine industry’s most critical challenges will be...
takeaways: Wine Australia has opened a competitive expression of interest for its Research & Innovation Fund, part of the Australian Wine Future Fund.
The Australian Wine Future Fund targets $50 million over five years from Commonwealth, state and private sources, complementing levy-funded research.
The EOI round closes 23 December 2026, with assessments in early 2027 and quarterly rounds thereafter.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting over 200 exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
Twelve national pavilions, including France, Italy and the United States, will show more than 1,000 wine and drinks brands.
Tariffs on some imported wines and spirits are set to fall as free trade agreements with Australia, UK, New Zealand and EU take effect.

MARKET.head: Australian white wine exports to China more than double in Q3 2026
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine export value to mainland China rose 1.9% in Q3 2026 while global exports fell 7.3%.
White wine export volumes to mainland China rose 143.6% in the quarter, per Wine Australia data.
White wine still made up only 7.14% of Australian export value to mainland China, against 91.62% for red.

CULTURE.head: Guardian tests universal wine glasses across budgets, with Jancis Robinson's design ranked top
CULTURE.summ:
Searching for a wine glass that can do it all? From short-stemmed to swirlable, dishwasher-friendly to delicate, here’s the glassware that’s a cut above the rest

• The best no- and low-alcohol wines for when you’re...
takeaways: Wine columnist tested universal wine glasses at various price points, judging aesthetics, aroma concentration, comfort and dishwasher safety.
A mouth-blown tulip glass designed with master of wine Jancis Robinson and Richard Brendon was rated the platonic ideal.
Robinson argues one glass shape suits all wines, including whites, sparkling and fortified wines, not just reds.

CULTURE.head: ProWine Shanghai shows China's wine buyers seeking distinctive, regional, casual-drinking wines
CULTURE.summ: China’s wine market is becoming more selective, more diverse and less dependent on formal drinking occasions, according to exhibitors at this year’s ProWine Shanghai
takeaways: Exhibitors at ProWine Shanghai say Chinese buyers are becoming more selective, seeking wines with distinctive character beyond quality and price.
The three-day exhibition drew over 620 wine and spirits exhibitors from 34 countries and regions, plus 21,800 trade visitors.
Wine drinking is widening beyond business banquets and gifting to casual restaurants, wine bars and drinking at home.

CULTURE.head: ASVO names Mark O'Callaghan and Lane Williams as new regional directors
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) has announced that the appointment of two new directors at its annual general meeting last week “strengthens the board's national presence and builds its depth of skill as the association moves into 2026/27”. “The new board comprises an excellent diversity of experience...
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology ratified four regional directors at its AGM for three-year terms.
Mark O'Callaghan, a Victorian winemaker and consultant, was appointed regional director for Victoria.
Lane Williams, head viticulturist at Leeuwin Estate, was appointed regional director for WA, QLD and Tasmania.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status slips as sales fall and mocktails outpace wine lists
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: Writer argues wine's once-shared social role is fading, as alcohol sales have fallen sharply in recent years.
Restaurant tables increasingly show fewer wine bottles, with some venues offering mocktail lists longer than their wine lists.
Writer draws a parallel to coffee, whose default status has given way to customised drinks at Starbucks and Dutch Bros.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business on Wine 101
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts this episode of the VinePair podcast Wine 101, featuring Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wine Cellars.
The conversation covers how Smith Story came to work in the wine business, framed as a casual talk about falling into the trade.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace and promotes the region's Riesling, Pinot Gris, Crémant d'Alsace and Pinot Noir.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical conductivity mapping to read vineyard soils
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity mapping from 2021 to guide soil pit digging.
The survey found limestone density differences about 1.5 meters down that were hard to see from the surface.
For the 2026 vintage, a tressed Pinot Noir parcel reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for a trimmed neighbor.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its Agrochemical and MRL Search app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its free Agrochemical & MRL Search app.
The app gives rapid access to information from the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the 'Dog book'.
Users on Apple App Store and Google Play Store are asked to update the app to keep receiving updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography’s 2026 Gift Guide for Discerning Wine Lovers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Buying a gift for a serious wine lover can be maddening. The more devoted they are, the better the odds
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau was pushed onto the world stage by Beaujolais vignerons, with négociant Georges Duboeuf marketing it beyond France from the 1970s.
Lapierre in Morgon labels its new red a Vin de France called "Raisins Gaulois" because cru-designated wines cannot carry the Beaujolais Nouveau name.
Ca' del Bosco in Franciacorta runs an elaborate "grape spa" that washes and dries grape clusters before fermentation, as Jamie Goode documents.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast named California's Livermore Valley its 2026 American Wine Region of the Year in its annual Wine Star Awards.
Livermore Valley is known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, which its regional association named its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Blanc de Noirs Champagnes are white wines made from black grapes, since Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier have colourless juice and pigment only in the skins.
Garnacha Tintorera (Alicante Bouschet) is a red-fleshed teinturier grape bred in 19th-century France by Louis and Henri Bouschet to add colour to wines.
The featured Pago Casa Gran 'Reposo' 2024 from Valencia, Spain, is a blend of 60% Garnacha Tintorera, 20% Syrah and 20% Monastrell.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Eight impressive wines from leading independent wine merchant Yapp Brothers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Yapp Brothers are based in Wiltshire, in the southwest of the UK, and are an important importer of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Yapp Brothers, a Wiltshire-based importer and independent merchant, showcased eight wines at the Bunch tasting, a collaborative event of independent retailers.
Domaine André Vatan Sancerre Les Charmes 2025 is rated 94/100 at £23.25, described as a benchmark despite the warm year.
Patrick Jasmin Côte-Rôtie La Giroflarie 2022 earned the top score of 95/100 at £52.75, alongside Jasper Hill Georgia's Paddock Shiraz 2023 at 94/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What the Hell Do They Mean?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Let’s play wine tasting note bingo, here’s TMC’s handy guide
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: It says 'minerality' has a 'good' and 'bad' variant, and claims 'bad minerality' doesn't exist, while 'the new minerality' is speculated to mean leaner, high-acid wines.
The author says 'funky' and 'dilute' are used as descriptors, with 'dilute' a red flag for €500 Chambolle-Musigny buyers and 'funk' reportedly banned in Berlin and New York.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
The Mâconnais's bulk Mâcon-Villages Blanc price fell 9 per cent and Bourgogne Blanc fell 13 per cent, per regional figures reported in March.
Pouilly-Fuissé was valued at about €817 a hectolitre for the 2024 harvest, versus about €3,050 for Puligny-Montrachet.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics' expertise should be just slightly above their target audience's level, not necessarily supertasting or deep scholarship.
Atkin says disclosing pay-to-play arrangements is useful, but calls theatrical displays of chastity about conflicts of interest less interesting.
Atkin criticises the typical 30-second tasting of wines, often in lineups of tens or over a hundred, as too little time to judge a wine properly.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and private cellar sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or uploaded images, and Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available and connects them with sellers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy and about a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain dropped to sixth for value in China, below New Zealand, with a per-liter value only above Chile among the top eight sources.
The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with a Guangzhou stop on November 6, showcasing value wines including DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo.
